digest.component_or_area: Jira Data Center adapter transport on pycontribs/jira
propositions: The DC transport must implement TicketTransport, SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, and SupportsAbsenceProbe roles using pycontribs/jira as a maintained client library, with every method returning raw payload shapes (dicts) not jira.Issue objects so downstream mappers are unaffected.

Configuration must enforce HTTPS for non-loopback base_url unless allow_insecure=true is set; certificate verification must never be disabled via verify=False; ca_bundle must be supported for internal CAs; resolved_statuses must be configurable since self-hosted DC workflows use non-Cloud-standard names.

Authentication uses Personal Access Token (DC 8.14+) read from JIRA_PAT env-only, passed as bearer token_auth; a malformed [tool.rebar.jira] config must raise ConfigError rather than degrade to env-only, with the library import confined to an opt-in [jira-datacenter] extra and imported lazily so 'import rebar' stays dependency-free.

Retry policy must mirror acli_rest exactly: retry transient faults (ConnectionError, Timeout, TimeoutError) with 2s/5s backoff but never retry HTTP errors; unknown assignees raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError; the self-registration import in adapters/__init__.py is required so select_backend('jira-datacenter') finds the registered backend.

All TicketTransport, SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, and SupportsAbsenceProbe methods must pass live tests against the J5 harness with every postcondition verified on the server; NameIdentity user-search resolver must return authoritative identity for real DC users and raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError for unknown ones.

The pycontribs/jira version must be pinned with compatible-release bound (e.g. jira>=3.8,<4); raw payload shapes must conform to the shared _jira_shape_contract assertions (same functions used by Cloud fake and Cloud real tests); no changes under adapters/jira/acli*.
